# Use exec-summary

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Compress a long technical document, design doc, or proposal into a one-page executive summary aimed at non-technical or time-poor stakeholders.

**Reach for it when** the user has a long doc and needs a 30-second readable version, or is writing a 1-pager for a steering committee, partner, or executive sponsor.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install exec-summary                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install exec-summary --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install exec-summary --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Stakeholder comms pack: [`--pack stakeholder-comms`](../packs/use-the-stakeholder-comms-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Summarize this design doc for our executives"
- "I need a one-page summary of this long proposal for a non-technical stakeholder"
- "Give me the 30-second version of this technical document"
- "Compress this into something our COO will actually read"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Build me a PowerPoint of this"
- "Outline the slides for this presentation"
- "What should I change about how I present to a board audience?"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use exec-summary".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Quantify or qualify.** Numbers are best ("\$2.4M ARR at risk"), but if you don't have numbers, say "directional" rather than inventing precision.
- **Plain language.** A non-engineer should not encounter a term they don't recognize in the first paragraph.
- **No internal-team-speak.** "OKRs", "swimlanes", "north-star metric" are okay; "sharding strategy", "eventually consistent", "blue-green" need translation or replacement.
- **Active voice, second person where natural.** "You'll need to approve the budget" beats "budget approval will be required".
